mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over the prior month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% month-on-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day average during the same rate hike phase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs month-on-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Over 10 out of 12 months with such labor signals, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests expanding economic demand, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During 20 consecutive months of INDPRO > 2% monthly growth, 20-day forward returns are not higher than the prior month's 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both CPIAUCSL inflation and GDPC1 goods demand suggests a supply-side easing that reduces growth fears, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 days in a non-recessionary regime.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 205 and GDPC1 < 11600 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During 15 such supply easing months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for three consecutive months without a corresponding drop in UNRATE, it indicates persistent monetary tightening that raises discount rates and suppresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% for three consecutive months and UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative across 5 such regimes (average p-value > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) followed by a sharp decline in unemployment (UNRATE) creates a labor market surprise that temporarily boosts risk appetite, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 50,000 jobs in a single month while UNRATE falls by > 0.3 percentage points
failure_condition: Across 8 such events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RSAFS demand metrics while FEDFUNDS remains unchanged suggests underutilized monetary policy, which can lead to higher real rates and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days in a recessionary context.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by > 5% month-over-month for two consecutive months and FEDFUNDS is flat
failure_condition: During 10 such episodes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% and INDPRO grows by over 3% for two consecutive months, it indicates a supply-side improvement that reduces growth concerns and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days in a non-stagflationary regime.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and INDPRO > 112.5 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 8 such supply signals, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).
